messages:
oliver: Noticed a subtle slug collision during the migrate/docs-v2 rework. Headings with acronyms like "APIv2" turned into inconsistent anchors depending on the generator (apiv2 vs api-v2). CI linkcheck flagged user docs linking to API reference.

ci-bot: linkcheck: 3 failed fragments
- /docs/reference/api-generate#apiv2 -> 404 (fragment not found)
- /docs/guides/migrate#python-snippets -> 404 (fragment not found)
- /docs/examples/auth#key-rotation -> 200 but redirected -> warn

jisoo: Ugh. This is the slugify mismatch between mkdocs-material and docusaurus. One strips camelcase into lowercase run-on, the other inserts hyphens at camel boundaries. We should prefer explicit header ids when the heading contains acronyms or punctuation.

pat: I prototyped a small grep/replace script that scans for headings with ALLCAPS or camel acronyms and adds an explicit id if missing. Example:
```markdown
## APIv2 examples {#api-v2-examples}
```
This would make links stable regardless of slug policy.

oliver: Nice. Can you make it a GH action that runs on docs/* changes and bails CI if a heading likely to change slug lacks an explicit id? We should fail fast instead of letting a PR land.

pat: Yep. I'll add a lightweight action that looks for headings matching /[A-Z]{2,}|[a-z][A-Z]/ and ensures curly-id suffix exists. It only modifies PR branches in a lint commit if allowed.

nora: One other weirdness: snippets that begin with a Markdown blockquote char (">") or a leading "@" decorator get treated differently by MDX and that changes the AST which in turn changes nearby heading ids. We hit it when a snippet started with "> Note:" and the generated id lost a trailing token. Wrapping those snippets in a raw block or forcing fenced language seems to fix it.

jisoo: Agreed. Add guidance to contributors.md: prefer explicit language markers (```python), avoid leading punctuation-only lines in top-level headings, and use explicit {#ids} when anchors are consumed by automation.

ci-bot: FYI: re-run linkcheck after commits with `npx linkinator ./build --fragment` or use the GH action preset.

pat: I'll open PR with 3 pieces: the slug-lint GH action, a one-off patch adding explicit ids to ~6 affected headings, and a short notes patch in contributors.md. I will also include a tiny redirect map for the heaviest-hit old anchors to ease the migration.

oliver: Thanks. Can we also add a short test that builds the site and asserts that all internal anchors referenced in docs/*.md exist in the HTML output? We had false positives when links were redirected which still return 200.

pat: Good call. I'll make the check verify fragment presence in the built HTML rather than only following the HTTP status.

nora: Optional: open an upstream issue mentioning the MDX behavior where leading punctuation inside code fences can affect AST/sluggen. I can draft it if you want.

jisoo: Please do, @nora. Link it from the PR for visibility.

oliver: Great. I'll hold merging the reorg until pat's PR lands and CI is green. Thanks team — this one was subtle but good to catch early. :mag:
